Nullus Engine/Getting started

GET STARTED / BUILD / EDITOR

Build Nullus and create your first project

Prepare a C++20 toolchain, build the Editor and Launcher from source, then create a scene and run a script.

What you need to build

Install Git, CMake 3.22 or newer, a C++20 compiler, and Python 3.8 or newer. The repository's global.json pins .NET SDK 8.0.408. CMake prepares a repository-local copy if it is missing.

  • Windows uses the Visual Studio 2022 MSVC toolchain and DX12.
  • Linux / WSL uses GCC or Clang and Vulkan. Check the build handbook for the Vulkan SDK version.
  • macOS uses Xcode and Metal. Runtime validation on devices is tracked separately.

Get the source and build

Clone the repository, then run the dependency preparation and build commands for your operating system. The first configuration may download third-party dependencies.

git clone https://github.com/NullusEngine/Nullus.git
cd Nullus

Windows · PowerShell

.\SetupDependencies.bat
cmake -S . -B build -G "Visual Studio 17 2022" -A x64
cmake --build build --config Debug --target Editor Launcher

Linux

./SetupDependencies.sh
./build_linux.sh debug

macOS

./SetupDependencies.sh
NLS_BUILD_TARGETS="Editor Launcher" ./build_macos.sh debug

See the environment and build handbook for output paths, dependency versions, and troubleshooting.

Create your first scene in the Editor

  1. Start the Launcher, choose a project name, location, and template, then open the project.
  2. Create a scene and objects in the Hierarchy. Edit components and transforms in the Inspector.
  3. Save the scene. Create a C# or Lua script in the Asset Browser and attach it to an object.
  4. Press Play, inspect the result in Game View, and check script output in the Console.

The first project guide includes complete steps for a camera, cube, and rotating script.

License and next steps

Nullus uses a custom Source-Available License that allows commercial and non-commercial games under its terms. Read the full license and contribution terms before using or contributing source code.
